title: How scope grows from a task to work across teams
captions: Early in your career, someone gives you a clear task: fix this bug, add this field. They have already decided what to build.
At mid-level, you own a feature for your team. The problem is defined, and you choose how to build it.
At senior, you own a project or a system. The problem is often unclear, so you define it, plan it and see it through.
At staff, the problem crosses many teams and lasts a year or more. You set direction more than you write code.
Each step adds scope, ambiguity and ownership. Your coding skill still matters. It is just no longer the whole job. Level names differ between companies.
